values.label: Phase 1: rev A hardware and firmware core
WP9 Rev B hardware and manufacturing

groups.description: 11 January to 16 April 2027. Ends with rev A boards running the new firmware on the test roaster, with the safety chain verified.
19 April to 9 July 2027. Ends with RC-2 rev A units roasting on the touchscreen, sending roasts to the cloud, syncing profiles with Studio and updating over the air.
12 July to 1 October 2027. Ends with rev B in hand, CE paperwork complete, three pilot roasteries running RC-2, and Ostler ready for series production.

data.title: Kick-off, phase plan and risk register
data.rationale: RC-1 kick-off took 30 h with the same customer and team; the new risk register format adds a little.

data.title: RC-2 requirements baseline
data.rationale: RC-1 spec took 62 h with two review rounds. About a third carries over unchanged; connectivity and the touchscreen are new.

data.title: Supplier and long-lead component management
data.rationale: 41 h on RC-1 against 8 estimated because of the MCU shortage. Allocation is calmer now; high keeps that case.

data.title: Phase 1 steering, reporting and change control
data.rationale: RC-1 ran at about 12 h a month (176 h over 15 months). 14 weeks plus the phase gate review.

data.title: Phase 2 steering and reporting
data.rationale: Same monthly rate as RC-1 (176 h over 15 months) for 12 weeks; no gate review inside the phase.

data.title: Phase 3 steering, reporting and close-out
data.rationale: Monthly rate from RC-1 (176 h over 15 months) plus the close-out report and final acceptance meeting.

data.title: Hardware architecture and board partitioning
data.rationale: RC-1 architecture took 26 h for a single board; the split into main and I/O board adds an interface to define.

data.title: MCU, wireless module and core schematic
data.rationale: 38 h on RC-1 for the MCU core alone. The wireless module adds antenna keep-out and RF supply work.

data.title: Thermocouple front-end, four channels
data.rationale: RC-1 two-channel front-end took 38 h. Channels three and four reuse the amplifier and cold-junction design, so about 1.3 times, not double.

data.title: Analog outputs: gas valve 4-20 mA and fan 0-10 V
data.rationale: RC-1 had the 4-20 mA output only (22 h); the 0-10 V fan output is a second, simpler channel.

data.title: Relay drivers and digital inputs
data.rationale: 24 h on RC-1; two more inputs (hopper and cooling tray) on the same pattern.

data.title: Power supply and input protection
data.rationale: RC-1 supply took 27 h; more load from the display backlight and the radio.

data.title: Display and touch interface
data.rationale: No comparable RC-1 work: RC-1 had a character LCD on a ribbon cable. Likely is from the display vendor's reference design; high allows for a backlight EMC problem.

data.title: PCB layout rev A
data.rationale: RC-1 layout took 92 h. Two boards and more nets, but a smaller analog section per board; about an eighth more.

data.title: Rev A build and bring-up
data.rationale: 71 h on RC-1, of which about 18 h was rework for a footprint error. Without it about 53 h; two boards to bring up, so 56.

data.title: Rev A characterisation
data.rationale: RC-1 took 30 h for two channels and one output. Four channels and two outputs, and Edda is new to the bench.

data.title: Enclosure adaptation and display mounting
data.rationale: RC-1 took 14 h for the enclosure alone. The touchscreen needs a front-panel cut-out, a bezel and a sourced cable.

data.title: Hazard analysis update
data.rationale: RC-1 hazard analysis took 36 h from scratch. RC-2 updates it for the supervisor MCU, remote access and OTA.

data.title: Interlock chain schematic
data.rationale: 28 h on RC-1. The chain is unchanged; the supervisor MCU tap-off points are new.

data.title: Supervisor MCU firmware
data.rationale: RC-1 watchdog took 30 h on the main MCU. A separate MCU adds its own build, the heartbeat protocol and safe-state tests.

data.title: Flame sensing and ignition sequence
data.rationale: RC-1 took 30 h; the logic is reused and moves to the supervisor.

data.title: Fault injection test rig
data.rationale: RC-1 had only a manual procedure (20 h, contractor). A rig with switchable faults is new hardware; weak analogue, wide range.

data.title: Interlock verification on the test roaster
data.rationale: 24 h on RC-1. The rig makes repeats cheaper, but there are more cases (supervisor faults).

data.title: Test plan and requirements traceability
data.rationale: RC-1 test plan took 24 h; more requirements and the connected features.

data.title: MCU port: board support and drivers
data.rationale: RC-1 bring-up took 48 h. New MCU family, so more than RC-1 even though the driver layer design is reused.

data.title: RTOS task structure and messaging
data.rationale: RC-1 used a cooperative scheduler (18 h). An RTOS is new for this codebase.

data.title: Temperature acquisition, filtering and rate of rise
data.rationale: 21 h for two channels on RC-1, plus 12 h for rate of rise (RC1-041). Filter and calibration code reused; four channels and a selectable rate-of-rise window.

data.title: Drum VFD driver over Modbus RTU
data.rationale: RC-1 took 118 h against 40 estimated because of the VFD firmware bug. Same VFD family and the workaround is documented, so 48; high keeps a new bug in mind.

data.title: Versioned settings storage with migration
data.rationale: RC-1 took 20 h without migration; RC-2 must read RC-1 settings and migrate on update.

data.title: Event and fault log
data.rationale: 14 h on RC-1; adds upload flags for the cloud.

data.title: USB-C service port and recovery mode
data.rationale: RC-1 USB log export took 24 h; recovery mode is new. Rui takes it because he wrote the host side.

data.title: Wireless module driver and connection manager
data.rationale: Nothing comparable in RC-1, which had no radio. From the module vendor's host driver example plus reconnect handling; high is a buggy vendor driver.

data.title: Firmware unit tests and CI
data.rationale: RC-1 set-up took 20 h; adds a hardware-in-the-loop runner for the supervisor.

data.title: Dual-bank bootloader with rollback
data.rationale: RC-1 USB bootloader took 22 h. Dual-bank with rollback is more logic; the image format is reused.

data.title: Burner PID control port
data.rationale: RC-1 PID took 34 h as a new design; this is a port with the same structure.

data.title: Profile follower
data.rationale: RC-1 follower took 40 h for one setpoint curve. RC-2 also follows airflow and drum speed events and must handle a late charge.

data.title: Airflow and drum speed scheduling
data.rationale: RC-1 had three relay steps for airflow (10 h); continuous airflow and drum speed are new outputs.

data.title: Roast phase state machine
data.rationale: 22 h on RC-1; same phases plus a preheat hold and the cooling handover.

data.title: Charge and drop detection
data.rationale: RC-1 turning-point detection took 18 h. Charge and drop detection need a recorded data set from three drum sizes.

data.title: Control tuning on three drum sizes
data.rationale: RC-1 tuning on the 5 kg drum took 24 h. Three sizes, most of the method carries over; high if the 15 kg drum needs gain scheduling.

data.title: Cooling and chaff cyclone control
data.rationale: 9 h on RC-1; adds the cooling tray stirrer timeout.

data.title: HMI flows and screen designs
data.rationale: RC-1 menu design took 12 h for a four-line display. Touch needs real screen designs, reviewed twice with Ostler.

data.title: Graphics library integration and display driver
data.rationale: RC-1 LCD driver and menus took 14 h. A graphics stack is a much bigger job; this analogue only anchors the menu engine part.

data.title: Live roast screen
data.rationale: The RC Logger live curve view took 38 h on desktop. Less library help on the MCU, but the curve logic ports.

data.title: Profile selection and manual override screens
data.rationale: 16 h on RC-1 as a menu; touch screens with a profile preview take longer.

data.title: Settings, service and diagnostics screens
data.rationale: RC-1 menus took 18 h; similar content on more screens.

data.title: Alarm display and acknowledgement
data.rationale: 8 h on RC-1; adds the alarm history list.

data.title: Touch usability test with three roasters
data.rationale: RC-1 session with two roasters took 14 h; three roasters and a short report.

data.title: Cloud architecture and hosting cost model
data.rationale: RC-1 licence server set-up took 14 h. This is a bigger decision, with a written cost model for Ostler.

data.title: Device provisioning and certificates
data.rationale: RC-1 licence activation took 30 h; per-device certificates add a factory step.

data.title: Telemetry ingest pipeline
data.rationale: Nothing comparable in RC-1. Based on Rui's 6 h spike in October 2026 that took one roaster's telemetry end to end.

data.title: Roast log storage and query API
data.rationale: The RC Logger local database took 34 h (partly reconstructed hours). Server-side storage and an API on top.

data.title: Profile library sync
data.rationale: RC-1 file import/export took 20 h. Two-way sync with conflict handling is the riskiest backend item.

data.title: Accounts, organisations and roles
data.rationale: RC-1 portal login took 16 h; organisations and three roles are new.

data.title: Service technician web console
data.rationale: RC-1 portal admin took 26 h. The console shows live status and logs per roaster, not just downloads.

data.title: Backend monitoring, backups and alerting
data.rationale: 10 h on RC-1 for one small server.

data.title: Security review and fixes
data.rationale: RC-1 review of the licence service took 16 h; much larger attack surface now. Edda leads it, Rui fixes.

data.title: Studio on the RC Logger codebase
data.rationale: The RC Logger skeleton took 28 h; we refactor rather than rewrite.

data.title: Live view over the network
data.rationale: RC-1 USB live connection took 30 h; network discovery and the cloud relay path are added.

data.title: Profile editor
data.rationale: RC-1 point editor took 44 h. Adds airflow and drum speed lanes and validation against roaster limits.

data.title: Roast comparison and overlay
data.rationale: 18 h on RC-1; reads cloud logs instead of local files.

data.title: Installers, code signing and auto-update
data.rationale: RC-1 took 22 h including two days lost to macOS notarisation, which we now know; auto-update is new.

data.title: OTA client in firmware
data.rationale: The RC-1 bootloader (22 h) is the closest work. Download, signature check and swap sit on top of the WP3-10 bootloader.

data.title: OTA release service and staged rollout
data.rationale: RC-1 firmware download portal took 24 h; staged rollout and rollback reports are added.

data.title: Image signing and key management
data.rationale: No RC-1 equivalent; RC-1 images were unsigned. Includes the key ceremony and the procedure for Ostler's production line.

data.title: Telemetry client with offline buffering
data.rationale: RC-1 USB stick export took 22 h; buffering and resume after a dropout are most of the work.

data.title: Wi-Fi setup over Bluetooth from a phone
data.rationale: The cancelled RC-1 Bluetooth display reached 14 h, so BLE stack bring-up is partly known. Weak analogue.

data.title: End-to-end connected test
data.rationale: RC-1 system test took 40 h for 12 roasts; RC-2 runs 20 roasts with dropout scenarios.

data.title: OTA failure-mode tests
data.rationale: Comparable to the RC-1 interlock verification (24 h): a fixed list of cases (power loss, bad image, dropout) repeated on the bench.

data.title: Rev B change list, schematic and layout
data.rationale: RC-1 rev B took 64 h because an interlock relay was added late, plus 10 h for the findings list (RC1-080). We expect fewer changes, but two boards.

data.title: Manufacturability review with the contract manufacturer
data.rationale: 12 h on RC-1.

data.title: Rev B build of 20 units and bring-up
data.rationale: RC-1 rev B build of 12 units took 34 h; 20 units, but known boards.

data.title: Production test fixture
data.rationale: RC-1 fixture took 58 h for one board; two boards share one fixture with swappable plates.

data.title: BOM cost-down and second sources
data.rationale: 20 h on RC-1. Since the 2024 shortage Ostler wants a second source for every active part.

data.title: Production test firmware and factory provisioning
data.rationale: Petra's share of the RC-1 fixture was 6 of 58 h; loading device certificates at the factory (WP6-02) is new.

data.title: Compliance plan and standards list
data.rationale: RC-1 took 16 h; radio and cybersecurity rules join the list.

data.title: EMC pre-compliance and fixes
data.rationale: RC-1 took 52 h with one failed lab visit. Radio and display make a first-time pass less likely, so high stays wide.

data.title: Formal EMC and electrical safety test support
data.rationale: 30 h on RC-1; one more test day for the radio.

data.title: Radio conformity for the wireless module
data.rationale: RC-1 had no radio. The pre-certified module limits the work to integration tests and documentation if we follow its antenna rules.

data.title: Technical file and declaration of conformity
data.rationale: RC-1 took 26 h; more standards to reference.

data.title: Cybersecurity requirements for connected products
data.rationale: Closest RC-1 work is the licence service review (16 h). New to the team, though Edda has done it at her previous employer.

data.title: Firmware changes from EMC and radio findings
data.rationale: Part of the 52 h RC-1 pre-compliance work was firmware (clock spreading, edge rates); kept as its own item this time.

data.title: Pilot plan, site selection and agreements
data.rationale: RC-1 pilot plan for two sites took 12 h.

data.title: Pilot kit preparation, three kits
data.rationale: 16 h for two kits on RC-1.

data.title: On-site installation and commissioning, three sites
data.rationale: RC-1 installs took 30 h for two sites including travel, about 15 h a site.

data.title: Pilot support and remote monitoring, six weeks
data.rationale: RC-1 support took 28 h over four weeks without remote access. Remote monitoring makes each issue cheaper; more sites and weeks.

data.title: Pilot feedback analysis and fix list
data.rationale: 10 h on RC-1 for two sites.

data.title: Pilot fixes in firmware
data.rationale: RC-1 pilot fixes took 38 h for firmware and Logger together; the firmware share was 30 h. More features this time.

data.title: Pilot fixes in Studio and cloud
data.rationale: Rui's share of the RC-1 pilot fixes (38 h total) was 8 h; the cloud and Studio are much more surface.

data.title: Installation and wiring manual
data.rationale: RC-1 took 22 h (contractor); two boards and network set-up to add.

data.title: User manual for the touchscreen and Studio
data.rationale: RC-1 user manual took 24 h; two user interfaces now.

data.title: Service manual and troubleshooting guide
data.rationale: 16 h on RC-1; adds remote diagnostics.

data.title: Manufacturing release package
data.rationale: 14 h on RC-1.

data.title: Release 1.0 of firmware, Studio and cloud
data.rationale: RC-1 release took 14 h for firmware and Logger; three deliverables now.

data.title: Training for the Ostler service team
data.rationale: RC-1 training was one day (10 h with preparation); RC-2 is two days.

data.title: Production cloud environment, load test and runbook
data.rationale: RC-1 server set-up took 14 h. Production separate from staging, a 200-roaster load test and the operations runbook for Ostler's IT.
